newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mostly higher.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher, led by gains in silver, and helped by a rumor, later denied by officials, that Russian president Yeltsin had died, traders said.
"Precious metals month-long downtrend looks to have ended for now, but sideways looks to be the most likely direction from here," Mitsui USA bullion dealer Greg Drury said.

"Above the market there is central bank and producer selling, with the $385.00 level important for producer hedging, while below the market is good physical demand, so I wouldn't be a believer unless gold climbs over $386," he said.
COMEX December gold ended up 10 cents at $383.50 an ounce, after trading in a $382.60-384.40 range.

In New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted $381.05/381.55 an ounce, after seeing a session high around $381.90, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $381.35 and the New York close Tuesday at $381.10/381.60.
COMEX December silver ened up 7.5 cents at $4.973 an oucne, after seeing an intraday high at $4.995.
COMEX silver warehouse stocks, excluding Wilmington Trust silver stocks, stood at 137,631,324 ounces Tuesday, setting a new low for the year.
Wilmington Trust deliverable silver stocks fell 630,350 ounces to 58,782,969 ounces as of October 7. Wilmington Trust in Delaware becomes an official exchange silver depositary from January 1, 1997.
NYMEX January platinum ended up $2.20 at $391.20 an oucne, while NYMEX December palladium closed down 75 cents at $118.50.
Funds remained mostly positioned short in precious metals, analysts said, while better fabricator demand had been noticed in the past week, along with some buying of bullion by gold equities funds.
Based on the long-term nearby futures continuation charts, the outlook remained negative for precious metals, Prudential Securities technical consultant Jack Schwager said.

"The early 1996 high (at $417.50 in nearby gold futures) looks like a bear-trap top," he said in a monthly report. "A measured move based on the initial downswing from the 1996 high indicates a downside target near the $360 level."
In silver "although the price action remains negative, a plethora of technical factors suggest strong underlying support in the approximate $4.45-4.70 area, basis December," he said.

But since the decline in nearby silver futures in the past month took the contract down to 1996 low at only $4.80, the market remains well above this support and "Consequently (this will) allow for another downswing."
